extracted.intended_audience: All Texas law enforcement agencies; chief administrators and PIOs
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for Texas law enforcement agencies on designation, required training, certification, documentation, and reporting for Public Information Officers (PIOs) under HB 33 and related Texas Government Code provisions. Covers who must have a PIO, approved courses, timelines, and procedural steps to obtain and report TDEM certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies required to have a designated PIO
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the provisions of HB 33, certain law enforcement agencies are required to have a designated public information officer (PIO) (Texas Government Code § 411.3735). Those agencies subject to this requirement are: • A municipal police department, • A sheriff’s office, • A county constable’s office, • A school district police department, and • The Texas Department of Public Safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may serve as the PIO (chief administrator / peace officer status)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PIO may be the chief administrator but is not required to be a peace officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the chief administrator is the PIO, they must obtain the certification and complete the continuing education requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of certified PIOs required per agency
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency is only required to have one certified PIO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of PIO when not directly employed (policy/agreements/MOU)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PIO, if not directly employed by the chief administrator, should be clearly designated to the role through policy or written agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: a county PIO may, by written policy, act as the PIO for the sheriff’s office and the constables in the county; a school district PIO may, by written policy, be designated as the PIO for the school district police department. A small agency could obtain a Memorandum of Understanding where a PIO from a larger agency agrees to act as the PIO for both agencies. Agencies that designate an external PIO through policy or agreement must maintain a copy of that PIO’s proof of certification and continuing education with the agreement or policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and certification timing and continuing education requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The PIO must complete training and obtain a certification from the Texas Division of Emergency Management (TDEM) within one year of assignment to this position, and complete continuing education annually (Texas Government Code § 418.333).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals designated as a PIO currently have until September 1, 2026, to complete this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of certification and continuing education (inspection readiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: A PIO or their agency should be able to produce proof of certification and proof of continuing education (certificates) on inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies that designate an external PIO through policy or agreement must maintain a copy of that PIO’s proof of certification and continuing education with the agreement or policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved courses that satisfy TDEM certification
rubrics_metrics.description: The currently approved courses to obtain TDEM certification are (TCOLE number — Course Name — FEMA/TDEM number where applicable): TCOLE 666038 — Bill Blackwood LEMIT Public Information Officer Course (FEMA/TDEM N/A); TCOLE 666318 — TEEX MGT 318 Public Information in All‑Hazards Incident (N/A); TCOLE 3763 — FBI LEEDA Media and Public Relations (N/A); TCOLE 3775 — FBI LEEDA Master Public Information Officer (N/A); TCOLE 667388 — FEMA/NIMS Advanced Public Information Officer (FEMA E‑388); TCOLE 667952 — FEMA/NIMS All‑Hazards Public Information Officer (FEMA E‑952); TCOLE 664033 — TDEM Texas Public Information Officer Course (T‑PUB4033).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links are provided for some courses; where FEMA/TDEM numbers exist they are listed. To obtain TDEM certification you must select and complete one approved course from this list.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to complete certification to TDEM (procedural steps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Steps to complete certification to TDEM:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1. Select and complete one approved course from the list above. 2. Save your completion certificate, ensuring your name and TCOLE PID are clearly displayed. 3. Upload your certificate to https://www.preparingtexas.org/. (Additional instructions referenced in the bulletin.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting training to TCOLE and TDEM
rubrics_metrics.description: You should report the training to TCOLE as you do all other training, and ALSO report the training to TDEM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TCOLE is working with TDEM to simplify this process so that PIO training, including certificate continuing education obligations, reported to TCOLE under a valid PID will automatically be reported to TDEM. This TAB will be updated once that process is finalized.
